document_title: Software pointed at a gene. Flies ran the test.
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Software did not diagnose this child.

The child was enrolled in the Texome Project. Standard analysis found no answer. Then AI-MARRVEL flagged a rare change in a gene called BRSK1.

That flag was a lead. Testing it took families and flies.

Through GeneMatcher the study grew to 10 affected people from seven unrelated families. In flies the gene is sff, for "sugar-free frosting." Switched off, the flies had trouble moving and lived shorter lives. The normal human gene largely corrected them. The three patient versions only partly did.

Every affected person had some developmental delay. Texas Children's calls the variants a likely diagnosis.

Texome takes candidates from underserved families with a suspected rare disease who can't pay. Testing is free and visits can be virtual. Could a family you know write to texome-project@bcm.edu?

#TexomeProject #TexasChildrens #BaylorMedicine

S1.headline: Software pointed at a gene. Flies ran the test.
S1.body: Researchers at Texas Children's and Baylor name variants in BRSK1 as a likely diagnosis for a rare disorder that had gone unexplained.
strings: Software pointed at a gene. Flies ran the test.
Researchers at Texas Children's and Baylor name variants in BRSK1 as a likely diagnosis for a rare disorder that had gone unexplained.

S2.headline: One child, and no answer.
S2.body: The child was enrolled in the Texome Project, which offers free genetic testing to medically underserved people with rare, undiagnosed conditions. Standard analysis of the child and a parent did not reveal an answer.
strings: The child was enrolled in the Texome Project, which offers free genetic testing to medically underserved people with rare, undiagnosed conditions. Standard analysis of the child and a parent did not reveal an answer.

S3.headline: Then software flagged BRSK1.
S3.body: AI-MARRVEL, a classifier trained on over 3.5 million variants, highlighted a rare change in BRSK1 as a promising candidate.
strings: AI-MARRVEL, a classifier trained on over 3.5 million variants, highlighted a rare change in BRSK1 as a promising candidate.

S4.headline: Ten people. Seven unrelated families.
S4.body: Shared through GeneMatcher, the finding drew in other families with rare variants in the same gene. Two of the ten had seizures.
strings: Shared through GeneMatcher, the finding drew in other families with rare variants in the same gene. Two of the ten had seizures.

S5.headline: A good pointer is still a pointer.
S5.body: On one confidence metric, AI-MARRVEL reached 98% precision and found 57% of diagnosable cases among 871. That is not its accuracy.
strings: A good pointer is still a pointer.
On one confidence metric, AI-MARRVEL reached 98% precision and found 57% of diagnosable cases among 871. That is not its accuracy.

S6.headline: With the gene off, the flies had trouble moving.
S6.body: The fly version of BRSK1 is called sugar-free frosting. Disabled, it also left the flies with shorter lives.
strings: With the gene off, the flies had trouble moving.
The fly version of BRSK1 is called sugar-free frosting. Disabled, it also left the flies with shorter lives.

S7.headline: The patients' versions only partly fixed the flies.
S7.body: The normal human gene largely corrected the flies. The team modeled three patient variants, and those restored the flies only partially.
strings: The patients' versions only partly fixed the flies.
The normal human gene largely corrected the flies. The team modeled three patient variants, and those restored the flies only partially.

S8.headline: A likely diagnosis. Not a certain one.
S8.body: Every affected person had some developmental delay. Common features included delayed speech and autism.
strings: A likely diagnosis. Not a certain one.
Every affected person had some developmental delay. Common features included delayed speech and autism.

S9.headline: Families who can't pay can ask.
S9.body: Candidates are underserved people with a suspected rare disease who can't pay for sequencing. Testing and follow-up are free, 5 visits in 2 years, in person or virtual. Write to texome-project@bcm.edu.
strings: Families who can't pay can ask.
